dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31-May cluster is a genuine month-end batch: 17 annual-plan (term_days=365) renewals that two West dealers, DLR-104 and DLR-219, posted together in one 21:00 run."
"The email's other reads — effective_event_date = dealer txn date, posted_at = month-end — match the lag pattern but rest on the email itself"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "West = DLR-104/219 is inferred, not in the data: recharges.csv has no region field"
"Revenue-recognition basis is not in these files"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single read-only check that could change the call: re-plot the May trend keyed on effective_event_date instead of posted_at"
"Do not reverse or hold any of these postings — they are unique, reconciled, real revenue."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Separately, confirm the recognition basis with Revenue Assurance and the West-dealer mapping in a dealer master before any external comment."
"If the spike persists on effective_event_date too, that would reopen it as a genuine month-end event surge."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "It is not duplicate, manipulated, or broken revenue." Uniqueness and reconciliation strongly address duplicate processing, but they do not by themselves rule out manipulated effective dates or establish customer entitlement/valid renewal status.
"they are unique, reconciled, real revenue." The files establish import and cash reconciliation, but the submission does not show an entitlement or contract-validity check.
"31-Jan 272, 2-Mar 266, 1-Apr 231, 30-Jun 217, 1-May 211 are all higher and all month boundaries." 2-Mar is not a month boundary, so this supporting characterization is factually overstated.

"if the 17 annual rows redistribute across their 1–28 May effective dates and 31-May stops being a peak, that confirms a posting-date artifact" Redistribution would support a posting-time explanation, but would not alone establish the complete absence of a material business or entitlement issue.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately handled the benign posting-time-batch interpretation and considered duplicate processing, manipulation, and pipeline failure. The main alternative left insufficiently tested is a genuine renewal or entitlement issue concentrated among the two dealers: import reconciliation and unique IDs show that files were processed once, but do not independently establish that every renewal was authorized and correctly entitled.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add an explicit entitlement check joining the 17 annual renewals to customer/account status, prior plan, renewal eligibility, and expected cash, and report the resulting match or exception counts before asserting that the postings are real revenue and safe not to hold.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell to index 59 in June while controls held ~100 (E 101, N 101, W 96); sessions ending at \"authenticate\" are 24.0% under NOVA vs 7.9% South-LEGACY / 6.9% other"
"tickets.csv → region + count by month(created_at)" and "ivr_interactions.jsonl → terminal_stage=\"authenticate\", grouped by pilot_version/region"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "the tripled pre-auth failures are would-be complaints that never became cases"
"Containment 64.8% (dashboard) vs 56.1% (all sessions); ~24% pre-auth sessions dropped from the denominator"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Inferences (tentative)" and "Unknowns: 7-day repeat-contact rate; the exact containment numerator/denominator; the operational fate of a pre-auth failure."
"New self-service stages balance_check (~29%) and pack_info (~21%) exist only under NOVA — some deflection is real"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally. Keep the South pilot running (reversible) but instrument it first"
"add pre-auth abandonment and all-contact containment to the dashboard, reconcile IVR sessions ... against cases ... and re-evaluate on a like-for-like metric"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Remaining unknowns that would change the call: the 7-day repeat-contact/callback rate ... the exact containment definition; and what operationally happens to a customer whose session dies at authentication."
"What are the exact numerator and denominator of the containment dashboard" and "Under NOVA-S1, what conditions create a case versus resolve-and-close versus transfer"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The South case drop is largely a measurement-and-authentication artifact, with a genuine but smaller self-service gain on top." The measurement failure is well supported, but a genuine CX gain is not established by the observed stage mix or case counts.

"the tripled pre-auth failures are would-be complaints that never became cases" is a plausible mechanism, but authentication abandonment is not itself evidence that the customer intended to complain or experienced worse friction.
"fix the named auth/prompt defects" is not supported by a clearly identified defect list in the submission; the questions identify possible error modes but do not establish confirmed defects.
"Person: Farah Iqbal ... she owns the IVR journey, the case-creation rules, and the containment metric" may exceed what the cited email establishes.
"South IVR sessions jumped ~12× ... a logging-regime change" is plausible, but the volume change could also reflect increased usage or pilot exposure unless the logging change is directly documented.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the alternative that some real self-service deflection exists, noting the NOVA-only balance_check and pack_info stages, while still rejecting national expansion. It does not fully preserve the benign interpretation that increased authentication abandonment could reflect users successfully completing an alternate journey or a logging/denominator artifact rather than failed complaint capture; journey linkage and sampled calls are needed to distinguish these possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Do not state that there is a genuine smaller self-service gain until linking IVR sessions to downstream outcomes. Obtain a session-level journey audit covering authentication failures, case creation, transfers, repeat contacts, callbacks, and sampled call recordings, then quantify all-contact containment and repeat-contact rates against a matched control.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the event count, dates, inverter IDs, and non-recurrence to “inverter_events.csv → all 4 rows; cols timestamp_local, inverter_id.”
It separately cites impact_mw, cleared, severity, and duration_min for the operational-status claim.
It explicitly distinguishes recorded values from what those values prove: “High (as recorded) / Low (as proof of no impact).”

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests the equipment-failure hypothesis against multiple recorded attributes: zero impact, cleared status, low severity, short duration, distinct inverters, and no repeat.
It recognizes an innocent data-quality explanation: “a uniformly-zero column can equally mean the field is unpopulated/defaulted.”
The analysis uses several fields from one CSV rather than truly independent channels, and it does not fully resolve whether impact_mw is actively computed.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Confidence is claim-specific: “High that the file records this; Low that it proves health.”
The completeness limitation is clearly stated: “I can't confirm from it alone that this is the full, unfiltered export.”
It proposes a bounded next check rather than escalating on weak evidence, while avoiding an assumption that additional data is already available.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: “Do not escalate” follows the observed zero impact, cleared events, short durations, and lack of recurrence.
The proposed completeness check is cheap and potentially decision-changing: confirm the date filter and plant-wide event count.
The recommendation to stop if the export is complete is somewhat stronger than the submission’s own caveat that impact_mw may be defaulted or unpopulated.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately says “Nothing in this file shows impact, recurrence, or an open fault,” rather than asserting that plant health is definitively proven.
It avoids inventing a plant problem from short communications or equipment-related warnings and appropriately treats the event wording as insufficient evidence for escalation.
The limited completeness check is consistent with the evidence and the stated uncertainty.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The wording is not evidence” is rhetorically too absolute: event names are not sufficient evidence of failure, but they can justify a low-priority quality check, especially because the names are mixed across communications, fan, and DC-input categories.

“If it is the full export, stop here” is slightly overstated given the submission’s acknowledgment that impact_mw could be unpopulated/defaulted; completeness alone does not validate that field’s semantics.
“No recurrence” is supported only conditional on the export being complete, a condition the submission correctly identifies but could repeat more explicitly in the conclusion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The events may be benign, short-lived telemetry or communications warnings, but the uniformly zero impact_mw values could also reflect a defaulted or uncomputed field. That alternative warrants validation of the field definition or population logic, not operational escalation based on the event names alone.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify that impact_mw is actively calculated and populated for these event types, ideally alongside the proposed plant-wide count/date-filter check; this would directly test the main remaining uncertainty behind the decision to stop.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission traces the 31.6% result to `dispatch_blocks.csv`, specifying `sum(dsm_penalty_rs)` by date and reproducing 662,444 to 453,086.
It identifies the same-day calculation fields: `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`, with `actual_mw` held fixed, and cites the 12 `schedule_source="pilot_revision"` blocks.
It distinguishes the observed arithmetic from causal interpretation: “the note's arithmetic is real, but ‘31.6%’ overstates what the pilot did.”

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission triangulates penalty totals, generation gaps, schedule fields, weather fields, firmware versions, DSM rate bands, and STOW state rather than relying on the headline.
It tests alternative explanations including fabrication, lack of a counterfactual, lower penalty versus commercial value, firmware confounding, and hindsight bias.
It identifies a plausible mechanism—lowering the schedule ahead of stow reduces deviation—while recognizing that the cross-day comparison is not a controlled causal estimate.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It limits the defensible result to “~17.5% on one weather-matched day” and explicitly rejects a general “31.6% pilot reduction.”
It states that generalization, ex-ante forecast skill, and net-value impact remain unidentified, and notes that the 4 June comparison is firmware-confounded.
It proposes the smallest decision-changing evidence: repeated high-wind days, a firmware-controlled comparison, net commercial value, and confirmation that revisions preceded observed generation.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “keep the pilot running as a low-cost evaluation” preserves possible operational value without expanding on a single day.
It appropriately recommends reporting the same-day repricing result rather than the cross-day headline and delaying scale decisions until replication.
The proposed shadow schedule, preregistered high-wind-day criteria, firmware control, and net-value measurement form a discriminating next test.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion directly satisfies the central causal distinction: the pilot day performed better, but the 31.6% cross-day difference is not an identified causal effect.
It retains a smaller positive result—approximately 17.6% from the same-day base-versus-submitted repricing—instead of overcorrecting to “no value.”
It correctly scopes the result to one pilot day and avoids claiming general effectiveness or positive net commercial value.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The within-day estimate is clean” is slightly too strong: matching mean wind, gust, and firmware does not rule out all same-day or block-level confounding, and the base schedule’s counterfactual status depends on the field semantics being correct.
“Base_schedule_mw is the ... no-pilot schedule” is treated as established from the data model; the submission appropriately flags the remaining need to confirm that the AI revision was ex ante.

“The mechanism ... is plausible” is reasonable, but the repricing calculation establishes the accounting effect of a lower schedule, not by itself the operational or causal effect of deploying an AI forecast.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.6% figure is a valid same-day accounting/repricing comparison, but it may not be a full causal estimate of AI forecast skill: the schedule was lowered on the pilot blocks, and the calculation holds actual generation fixed. The apparent benefit could therefore reflect the commercial rule's response to a lower submitted schedule, while energy value, timing, and any effects on generation remain unresolved. The 31.6% cross-day difference may additionally reflect the unusually severe 28 May event rather than pilot impact.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run repeated, preregistered high-wind events with the AI schedule and a contemporaneous base-schedule shadow, holding firmware and commercial rules constant, and evaluate both DSM penalty and delivered-energy value. Confirm from timestamped records that each schedule revision preceded the relevant generation and stow information.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared 90211000 = Swiss-approved P1001 code, current on the 2025-11-04 entry" tied to "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx → 'Swiss Matrix' P1001 row (Approved CN8, Effective From/To)"
"Flag value 90211090 = P1001's Helios commercial code, 'migration-mapped', 'not customs-ruling status'" tied to "product_master_current.xlsx → 'Read Me' sheet"
"Invoice Qty 10 but Line = Unit = CHF 126,900; AWB shows 4 pcs — separate valuation anomaly" tied to the invoice and air waybill

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "'90211000 is a keying error for 90211090.' Rejected — it is the jurisdiction-correct Swiss code, not a dropped digit."
"'Helios is the source of truth.' Rejected — it is commercial master data, migration-mapped, explicitly 'not customs-ruling status.'"
"'A mismatch flag = an error.' Rejected — with code-system/version unmodeled ... a differing string ≠ misclassification."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "I don't call it permanently clean, though: the matrix asks for Tares/ruling confirmation before legal use."
"The Swiss Tares entry / binding ruling ... is ... Decisive."
"Don't raise it to the broker as an error" is stronger than the stated uncertainty that the legally controlling Tares/ruling evidence is still missing.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Swiss local code ≠ EU CN8; 'matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected'"
"All variants share HS6 902110; they differ only in national digits 7–8."
"Helios is a commercial master data" field that is "migration-mapped" and "not customs-ruling status," which appropriately distinguishes system lineage from legal classification authority.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "The single read-only check that decides it: normalise both codes to HS6 ... 902110 == 902110 closes the flag as a cross-nomenclature artifact"
"the call changes only if a Swiss Tares lookup for P1001 returns a legally-required code other than 90211000"
"Separately, ask for the invoice's true quantity basis (not a code issue)."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No revenue at stake" is not fully established by a 0.0% duty rate and declaration-sourced preference/origin; taxes, fees, valuation consequences, or other liabilities are not addressed.
"No mismatch where it is harmonised" is too broad: HS6 agreement supports a nomenclature mismatch explanation but does not itself establish that the Swiss national classification is legally correct.
"The single read-only check that decides it" overstates the sufficiency of HS6 normalization, since the submission itself identifies a Swiss Tares/ruling confirmation as legally decisive.

"returns 90211000 → CONFIRMS no-escalation and closes it legally" may overstate what a matrix or lookup establishes unless the cited Tares/ruling is confirmed as binding and applicable to the transaction.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix or product mapping could be stale, nonbinding, or applied to the wrong product facts, while the flag may represent a required Swiss national code rather than a mere string mismatch. The submission partly addresses this by identifying missing Tares/ruling evidence, but it should preserve the possibility of a genuine declaration error until that evidence and product-classification basis are verified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the recommendation conditional rather than definitive: retain the no-escalation disposition as provisional, verify the applicable Swiss Tares or binding-ruling result and its product facts, and avoid treating HS6 equality alone as legally dispositive.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"The only Irish P1006 declaration, SUP-02, is expired: valid_to 2025-07-31 ... while the entry is dated 2025-09-18" tied to "supplier_origin_register.csv → SUP-02/P1006 row" and "supplier_declaration_reference.txt"
"Register silence ‘does not prove that no document exists outside the register’" tied to "supplier_declaration_reference.txt + origin-workshop.md"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "ERP shows US, so the claim is plainly false — reject it." Rejected as overreach
"The preference box being ticked means the claim is backed." Rejected — an indicator is an assertion
"The route into Ireland or the 0% rate settles origin." Rejected — a shipping lane and a duty rate say nothing about originating status
"this is ‘not established,’ not ‘disproven’"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "I stop short of calling it an error or fraud"
"the register lookup itself warns it ‘does not prove that no document exists outside the register’"
"A valid, in-date P1006 supplier / long-term declaration ... if one exists ... REVERSES the hold ... if none does, it CONFIRMS the hold"
"The single read-only check that decides it"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios records manufacturing country, not preferential origin"
"ERP records US manufacturing country and ‘was never designed to prove preference’"
"Which supplier actually sourced this consignment" is identified as missing
"The specific FTA/arrangement and the origin rule the broker invoked" is identified as missing
"Register ... is admittedly incomplete"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not grant preference on this evidence"
"request the actual originating-status proof and the rule invoked"
"fall back to non-preferential (MFN) if none appears"
"refer it as an error or fraud only if that verification is requested and comes back empty — not on a register gap alone"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The single read-only check that decides it" is overstated: a register lookup alone cannot decide preferential origin when the register is acknowledged to be incomplete and the applicable FTA, origin rule, supplier relationship, and consignment coverage also matter.

"A current Available qualifying declaration (an EU SUP-03/05/06 tied to this consignment) reverses the call to grant" is too categorical. A current supplier declaration may support the claim, but it does not by itself establish that the particular goods qualify under the applicable preferential-origin rule.

"only the expired SUP-02 or US-origin SUP-01 means the hold stands" omits other possibilities, including a valid declaration outside the register, a different sourcing supplier, or failure to establish the applicable arrangement and rule.

"fall back to non-preferential (MFN)" is operationally reasonable as a provisional control, but the submission does not establish whether MFN is legally or procedurally the correct treatment for this exact entry, especially given the stated 0.0% duty.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference flag could be a harmless or automatically populated data-entry indicator because the line is already declared US-origin at 0.0% duty, while a valid supplier declaration may exist outside the incomplete register. The available evidence therefore supports withholding preferential treatment pending verification, but not concluding that the claim is invalid or erroneous.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the proposed single-register check with a sequenced verification that obtains the actual supplier declaration for the consignment, confirms its coverage and validity on 2025-09-18, identifies the applicable FTA or arrangement and product-specific origin rule, and reconciles the result to the declaration and broker records.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "70.6% of qcore_release_ts values are stamped at exactly 02:10:00"; cites batch_release.csv and source_freshness.csv.
"73/262 (27.9%) are exceptions" and "42 HOLD rows have a null qcore_release_ts"; cites specific fields and the SOP.
"Arithmetic is clean: 0 negative durations, 0 lab-before-receipt"; cites timestamp fields.
"COA MISSING ... most likely CertVault nightly-index lag, not released-without-cert" is explicitly labeled as inference.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Cycle time depends on the clock" separates receipt-to-release from the SOP evidence-to-disposition clock.
"70.6% of release times are the 02:10 snapshot boundary" connects the timestamp pattern to a possible interface or snapshot mechanism.
"The data is broken — discard it" is rejected because arithmetic is internally clean while timestamp semantics remain uncertain.
"A live-QCore spot-check ... varying true times confirm the snapshot-default reading" identifies a discriminating test.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "this is my inference, not established" and "I hold this at Medium" appropriately calibrate the CertVault explanation.
"if 02:10:00 is a defaulted ... stamp ...; if QCore actually holds varying intraday disposition times ..." gives conditional decision logic.
However, "the intraday duration is fabricated for most rows" and "HOLD is a receipt-date artifact" are stronger than the cited timestamp concentration alone establishes.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "do not ship the cycle-time KPI from this extract yet" appropriately reframes the request around metric validity.
"Smallest verification: confirm what qcore_release_ts means ... plus a live-QCore spot-check" proposes a focused, reversible next step.

"An agreed metric definition — evidence→disposition, RELEASED only, open exceptions excluded — plus a fresher, source-aligned extract" is actionable, though the proposed cleaned routine-row statistic risks becoming a new KPI before event semantics are verified.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: Rejects "1.5 days is a real, trustworthy cycle time" using alternative clocks and the 02:10 concentration.
Rejects "The data is broken — discard it" using integrity checks while preserving a semantics hypothesis.
Rejects the COA control-breach interpretation and states that a live-portal check is needed.

The strongest competing explanation for the timestamp pattern is noted as a stale extract, but the submission does not fully test other explanations such as legitimate batch processing at a common release boundary.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "confirm what qcore_release_ts means via the data catalog plus a live-QCore spot-check of a handful of 02:10:00 batches" targets the smallest high-value evidence.
"A live-QCore spot-check of ~5–10 batches" specifies sample scope and gives the expected interpretation of varying versus uniformly-02:10 times.
"An agreed metric definition ... plus a fresher, source-aligned extract" directly addresses the SOP clock and the non-coherent LabTrack/QCore timing.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the intraday duration is fabricated for most rows" is not proven by concentration at 02:10 or by the daily-refresh metadata; it remains a strong hypothesis until the timestamp definition or event log is checked.
"HOLD is a receipt-date artifact" overstates a cohort pattern that could also reflect the extract cutoff or operational backlog; the causal explanation is not established.
Filtering out 02:10 rows and calling the remaining n=23 "routine rows that carry a real cycle time" may introduce selection bias and should not be treated as a validated process metric.
The COA/CertVault nightly-index explanation is appropriately labeled an inference, but the cited nightly cadence alone does not establish that it explains the 17 released rows.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent long cycle time may be a mixture of a legitimate or stale QCore interface/snapshot timestamp, non-coherent LabTrack and QCore extracts, and receipt-cohort censoring rather than a single fabricated timestamp mechanism. Some 02:10 timestamps could represent valid batch-release boundaries; an event or decision timestamp is needed to distinguish this from defaulting or delayed interface commits.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the QCore field definition and an event-level extract for a small stratified sample of 02:10 and non-02:10 records, including required-evidence-available, disposition-decision, and interface-commit timestamps, aligned to one snapshot. Use that evidence before reporting the cleaned 5.5-hour statistic or attributing the HOLD and COA patterns to artifacts.

"available_qty_global = -1 means no stock. Rejected — on-hand is 3 (belt) and 1 (seal)" — it separates retrieval from transferability and tests competing explanations, but does not fully incorporate stale data into the causal decision for the eight immediate actions.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Global stock view (MaintStar-global) dated 2026-06-26, refreshed monthly — ~4 weeks staler than the request export"
"Engineering 'already declined' the servo transfer ... I treat these as claims to verify, not proven facts"

"8 transfer-ready now" and "The firm saving is ~$20.5k" — confidence is generally claim-specific, but 'firm' savings and immediate readiness are too strong given the stale global availability snapshot.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing

"hand the 12 back each with its single open question, and keep buying the 4 servo drives"

"The new cross-site search is a lead generator, not a transfer authoriser" — the reframing is useful and prioritized, but cancelling POs and executing transfers before live availability and reservation confirmation creates avoidable operational risk.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The search found a match, so transfer it. Rejected"
"available_qty_global = -1 means no stock. Rejected"
"Same part family = interchangeable. Rejected"
"Pull the servo drives from the other plants. Rejected" — plausible alternatives are explicitly tested against stock, revision, restrictions, and email evidence, with future confirmation identified.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live-stock check on HA-0022 and ME-0006"
"Interchangeability sign-off for VLV-3722 rev A vs rev B"

"Whether any servo-drive reservation could safely be released ... plus written confirmation of Engineering's stated refusal" — the requests are targeted, prioritized, and tied to specific decision changes.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "8 transfer-ready now" and "The firm saving is ~$20.5k" are overstated while the MaintStar-global stock snapshot is about four weeks stale; these should be conditional candidate savings pending live availability and reservation confirmation.
"raise the 8 transfers and cancel those POs" is operationally premature without a final live-stock, reservation, qualification, and PO-cancellation confirmation step.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The eight apparent transfer-ready matches may be valid semantic and policy candidates but not currently actionable: stock, reservations, or site qualification may have changed since the stale MaintStar-global snapshot. The correct near-term conclusion could therefore be candidate generation with confirmation rather than immediate transfer execution.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Convert the eight 'transfer-ready' rows into conditional candidates and obtain a live, row-level stock/reservation and receiving-site qualification confirmation before authorizing transfers or cancelling POs; quantify the resulting confirmed rather than merely apparent savings.
